Contactless electroreflectance (CER) spectroscopy was used to study the built-in electric fields and Fermi level positions in GaN/(Ga,Mn)N heterostructures.
The Fermi level in (Ga,Mn)N with Mn concentrations above 0.1% was found to be strongly pinned in the middle of the band gap, around 1.25 - 1.55 eV above the valence band.
The Fermi level position did not show a strong dependence on the thickness of the GaN capping layer, indicating it is predominantly determined by the bulk properties of the (Ga,Mn)N layer.
As the Mn concentration increased, the Fermi level moved deeper into the band gap, from closer to the conduction band at low x to the middle of the gap at higher x.
The researchers estimated that most of the band gap change in (Ga,Mn)N compared to GaN takes place in the valence band, amounting to a decrease of 0.028 ± 0.008 eV per % of Mn.
The strong mid-gap Fermi level pinning and lack of a surface depletion layer make (Ga,Mn)N a promising insulating buffer material for GaN-based transistors and other high power devices.
The (Ga,Mn)N layers studied were highly resistive, with a dielectric strength of 5 MV/cm, indicating their suitability as insulating buffer layers.
The Fermi level position was determined by analyzing the period of Franz-Keldysh oscillations observed in the CER spectra of the GaN/(Ga,Mn)N structures.
Two sets of samples were grown by molecular beam epitaxy, one with a constant 60 nm GaN cap and the other with varying GaN cap thicknesses from 31 to 170 nm.
Single (Ga,Mn)N layers were used as reference samples to support the analysis of the bilayer structures.
